mainEntity.name: How much does a Mini Countryman Cooper SD engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mini Countryman Cooper SD engine replacement costs typically range from £1,400 to £3,200 for a rebuilt N47D20C unit. Rebuilt units offer the best balance of reliability and value for most UK owners seeking long-term solutions without main dealer pricing.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mini Countryman Cooper SD?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mini Countryman Cooper SD timing chain failure stems from the rear-mounted tensioner design losing hydraulic pressure during cold starts. The chain stretches, guides shatter, and valves can collide with pistons.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Mini Countryman Cooper SD and Cooper D engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mini Countryman Cooper SD uses the twin-turbo N47D20C engine producing 143hp, while the standard Cooper D uses the single-turbo N47D20A producing 112-143hp.

historyTimeline.h2: Mini Countryman Cooper SD - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Mini Countryman Cooper SD launched, it brought high-performance sequential twin-turbo diesel capability to the premium crossover range. Throughout its lifecycle, this specific variant was exclusively powered by the robust but complex 2.0-litre N47D20C engine architecture.

milestones.description: N47D20C, 2.0L, 143hp (R60 generation launch, available in both front-wheel drive and ALL4 configurations)
Minor software and emissions mapping updates to the N47D20C to improve DPF regeneration cycles and throttle response.
End of R60 production; the Cooper SD badge and the N47D20C engine were discontinued for the subsequent F60 generation.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mini Countryman Cooper SD is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mini Countryman Cooper SD Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mini Countryman Cooper SD delivers strong twin-turbo diesel performance, but the N47D20C engine has specific, well-documented wear points. Timing chain degradation and turbo wastegate faults account for the majority of Mini Countryman Cooper SD replacement requests. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded tensioners and revised components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the Mini Countryman Cooper SD N47D20C Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mini Countryman Cooper SD / SD ALL4 (N47D20C, 2010-2016)
problems.rootCause: The rear-mounted timing chain design relies on a single hydraulic tensioner that loses pressure during cold starts. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides shatter, risking catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removes sump and valve cover, installs upgraded metal tensioner, revised guides, and new chain.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if chain stretch is under 1% and no internal damage has occurred.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete unit swap featuring factory-spec assembly, upgraded timing chain kit, and bench-tested compression. Includes 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the chain has jumped time, damaged valves, or if bottom-end bearings show wear.

problems.recommendation: If your Mini Countryman Cooper SD exhibits early cold-start rattle under 80,000 miles, a preventative timing chain kit replacement is the most cost-effective route. However, if the chain has jumped time or the turbo has failed catastrophically, a rebuilt N47D20C engine with upgraded tensioners delivers far better long-term reliability than a partial top-end repair.

problems.h4: Turbo Wastegate & EGR Cooler Failure - Twin-Turbo Stress on the Mini Countryman Cooper SD
problems.affectedModels: Mini Countryman Cooper SD / SD ALL4 (N47D20C, 2010-2016)
problems.rootCause: The sequential twin-turbo setup places high thermal stress on wastegate pivot bearings, causing boost leaks. Concurrently, soot-laden exhaust gases cause micro-fractures in the EGR cooler weld seams, leading to coolant loss.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - EGR Cooler & Turbo Actuator Replace
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Drops intake manifold, replaces cracked cooler with updated OEM part, and replaces faulty turbo actuators.
repairOptions.longevity: Restores factory emissions compliance and boost. Suitable if no coolant has entered the combustion chambers.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with updated EGR piping, revised thermostat housing, and new cylinder head gasket. Includes 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix for hydrolocked or contaminated engines. Upgraded EGR routing prevents repeat fractures.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. A typical R60 Mini Countryman Cooper SD (2010-2016) currently falls into the £4,000-£7,000 value band. Therefore, a quality used engine or targeted timing chain/turbo repair is often the most economically sensible route, as a full rebuild may approach or exceed the vehicle's total market value. Evaluate scrap or part-exchange value first if the chassis shows significant wear.
problems.recommendation: If your Mini Countryman Cooper SD exhibits early cold-start rattle under 80,000 miles, a preventative timing chain kit replacement is the most cost-effective route. However, if the chain has jumped time or the turbo has failed catastrophically, a rebuilt N47D20C engine with upgraded tensioners delivers far better long-term reliability than a partial top-end repair.

items.question: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mini Countryman Cooper SD?
items.answer: Mini Countryman Cooper SD timing chain failure stems from the rear-mounted tensioner design losing hydraulic pressure during cold starts. The chain stretches, guides shatter, and valves can collide with pistons.

Check engine light or loss of power due to incorrect valve timing.

items.question: What is the difference between the Mini Countryman Cooper SD and Cooper D engine?
items.answer: The Mini Countryman Cooper SD uses the twin-turbo N47D20C engine producing 143hp, while the standard Cooper D uses the single-turbo N47D20A producing 112-143hp.

The twin-turbo setup places additional thermal stress on the EGR cooler and wastegate actuators.
Replacement parts and rebuilt units are specific to the N47D20C code and are not interchangeable with the N47D20A.
